2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the petitioner as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1998 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act impleading the respondents as pre-emptees which was dismissed by the trial Court but on appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 83 of 2003 the lower Appellate Court reversed the decision of the trial Court and allowed pre-emption in favour of the pre-emptor. 

 9. Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the trial Court after proper appreciation of evidence on record arrived at a finding that the appellant is not a cultivator and he does not come within the meaning of a raiyat and, as such, the pre-emption case is not maintainable and this finding of the trial Court has not been reversed by the, appellate Court and the High Court Division has rightly dismissed the miscellaneous case holding that the pre-emptor not being a cultivator is not entitled to pre-empt the case land. He further submits that the trial Court after proper appreciation of the evidence on record came to a definite finding that proforma-respondent No. 2 offered the appellant to purchase the case land, but he expressed his inability and the appellate acted as mediator in the transfer of the holding and the appellate Court reversed the finding of the trial Court on the ground that the assertion on waiver and acquiescence made by OPW2 has not been corroborated by other witnesses and the High Court Division on perusal of the pleadings, the evidence on record and the judgment of both the Courts blow came to the finding that the finding of the appellate Court is totally based upon misconception of law and fact and also based on misreading as well as non-consideration of the material evidence on record as the pre-emptee has taken the plea of waiver and acquiescence in his pleadings and that the evidence of OPW2 has been corroborated by OPW1 and OPW3 and that the statement made by OPW1 in course of cross-examination that the seller told him that he offered the pre-emptor to purchase the case land has not been challenged by the pre-emptor and the testimony of OPW3 on this point has also not been challenged by the pre-emptor. He further submits that the appellate Court on misconception of law and fact and upon misreading and non-consideration of material evidence on record reversed the finding of the trial Court on the point of waiver and acquiescence and the High Court Division has rightly set-aside the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court and affirmed the same passed by the trial Court.
